# honeybadger_project_key (Resource)

A Project Key: what an app sends errors and events with, set as `api_key` in a notifier's config. It only sends data; reading or managing anything through the API takes an API Token. Required scopes: `projects:read`, `projects:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "honeybadger_project_key" "deploy" {
  project_id = honeybadger_project.app.id
  label      = "deploys"
}

# The app reports errors with this Project Key. It isn't a secret: it ships
# in the app, so it can go into the app's config as is.
output "deploy_project_key" {
  value = honeybadger_project_key.deploy.key
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (String) The project's `id`, as a project read returns it.

### Optional

- `label` (String) Optional human-readable name.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the key was created
- `id` (String) Identifier for this key. Use it in paths.
- `key` (String) The Project Key value a notifier sends. Returned in full: unlike an API Token, it's meant to ship with your application.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = honeybadger_project_key.deploy
  id = "<project_id>/<id>"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import honeybadger_project_key.deploy "<project_id>/<id>"
```
